To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. The four-fermionic cross sections for the processes e + e − → f f f f, e + e − + γ → f f f, and e + e − (γ) → Z f f f are calculated in the Standard Model at next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO) and in the Standard Model

the four-fermionic processes are the most important processes for the production of Higgs bosons in the intermediate Higgs mass range, 100 GeV ≤ M H ≤ 140 GeV, and that the four- fermion processes have to be included for an accurate description of the Higgs boson signal in the intermediate mass range.

the next-to-leading-order corrections to the four-fermionic cross sections are of the order of 10% for all processes and that the four-fermi cross sections are not sensitive to the choice of the renormalization and factorization scale.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a systematic study of the four fermion processes in e ^{+} e ^{-} collisions, with particular emphasis on the Higgs production and decay modes.

the study of the properties and the dynamics of the hadronic matter in the high energy regime, where the fundamental theory of strong interactions, QCD, predicts that quarks and gluons, rather than nucleons, are the relevant degrees of freedom.
the development of the next generation of particle detectors, the NEXT experiment, based on the detection technique of the electroluminescence (EL) of noble gases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present situation of the theory of the weak interactions is not satisfactory and that it should be improved by including the strong interactions.
the Higgs boson mass lies in the range 114.4– 185.6 GeV at the 95% confidence level.

the next-to-leading order QCD corrections for Higgs production in gluon fusion are very large, of the order of 100%, and the corresponding uncertainty in the theoretical prediction of the total cross section is large as well.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have implemented a complete set of processes for e + e − annihilation into four fermions in the standard model.
the program NEXTCALIBUR is now ready to use.
we have completed a four-fermions generator for e + e − annihilation that can handle all four-fermi final states.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the absence of a Higgs boson, the dominant contribution to the four-fermionic cross sections comes from t -channel exchange of W bosons.
, for all four-fermi processes, the next to next to leading order (NNLO) corrections are of the order of the leading order (LO) ones.
the Higgs boson is produced in a large variety of channels, which makes it difficult to identify.
